newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN staff remember colleagues killed in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: UN staff remember colleagues killed in Rwanda.

text.p: Several hundred United Nations staffers and aid workers gathered at the European headquarters in Geneva on Monday to commemorate five human rights staffers killed by gunmen in Rwanda last week.

"We are profoundly shocked by this tragedy, this act of violence against the defenceless and unarmed whose only aim was to respect and promote human rights," U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Jose Ayala Lasso said at the ceremony.
"Their deaths must not go unpunished. Those responsible must be brought to justice," he said.

Unidentified assassins killed four U.N. human rights monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- in an ambush last Tuesday in Cyangugu in southwestern Rwanda. Their Rwandan driver later died of his wounds.
The Briton, 36-year-old Graham Turnbull, was buried near his home in York at the weekend, friends who attended the funeral said.

Turnbull was team leader for human rights observers in Cyangugu. He had only recently warned his colleagues about the growing dangers in the region, where Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army is fighting majority Hutu rebels.

He was engaged to a Rwandan and they were planning to get married soon. His staff have criticised Ayala Lasso for not going to Rwanda immediately after the killings and for not attending Turnbull's funeral.

A wave of attacks targeting aid workers in Rwanda have underlined the vulnerability of relief staff in conflict zones and triggered a crisis of conscience and confidence at the Geneva headquarters of humanitarian agencies.

Aid officials say new security answers are needed to deal with new dangers caused by a surge in insurgencies around the world and the spread of arms since the end of the Cold War and its particular balance of power as a source of order.
